title: What Building Passport Systems Is
definition: Building Passport Systems: passports tracking building materials.
description:
Building Passport Systems is passports tracking building materials. It sits squarely in Future Architecture & Building, the frontier where material IDs science becomes system logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are renovation-scale. Societies that master system hulls early will shape BIM integration practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why material IDs programs worldwide now treat Building Passport Systems as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Building Passport Systems needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

t: Real Research Today: Building Passport Systems
title: Real Research Today: Building Passport Systems
definition: Today's documented research behind Building Passport Systems.
description:
The road to Building Passport Systems is already being paved. Mass timber towers (Mjøstårnet Norway, Ascent Milwaukee) prove tall wood buildings. Bamboo construction research (INBAR) standardizes the world's fastest-growing structure.

The New European Bauhaus fuses sustainability with design culture. Together these programs form the material IDs foundation that Building Passport Systems will build on — the system logistics results, the BIM integration methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as system logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First system hulls districts certified: material IDs assembly at
definition: 2030 milestone on the Building Passport Systems roadmap.
description:
First system hulls districts certified: material IDs assembly at half the time and carbon of legacy builds.

What must be true first: the material IDs results have to replicate outside the lab, system logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and BIM integration operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed material IDs demonstrations, system logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting BIM integration uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Building Passport Systems
definition: Estimates Building Passport Systems readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Building Passport Systems components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a system hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Building Passport Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Building Passport Systems operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Building Passport Systems installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 90036 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where material IDs monitoring, system logistics redundancy, or BIM integration maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Building Passport Systems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Building Passport Systems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Building Passport Systems — passports tracking building materials.

Phase 1 — Prove (material IDs): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (system logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (BIM integration): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (renovation): system hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and buildings-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
